title: ci: run gen's tests before the migration, not after it
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- `deploy-gen` ran gen's `Test`/`Typecheck` after `migrate`, putting ~2.5 min between the schema moving and gen deploying. Measured on the first unified run: schema live 17:30:00, gen live 17:33:24.
- During that gap the deployed gen queries the old schema. `loadGenerationModelRegistry` has no try/catch around `getCommunityModelRegistryEntries`, so a removed column fails the whole registry build — `STATIC_ENTRIES` too. All image and text traffic 500s, not just community models.
- Hoists `Test`/`Typecheck` into a `test-gen` job gating `migrate`. `deploy-gen` becomes install + deploy (~30s with the npm cache), inside `REGISTRY_TTL_MS = 60_000`, so the cached registry can cover the window.
- Side effect worth having: a red gen test now blocks the migration instead of trailing it. Previously the migration was test-gated only when gen won the race — 1 of 3 orderings.
- `migrate`'s `if` needs `!cancelled()`; without a status function a skipped `test-gen` (gen not deploying) would skip `migrate` and every deploy with it.
- Couples the release: a gen test failure now blocks enter and media too. Intended — they share one schema.

gist.headline: Tests Before the Soil Moves
gist.blurb: The hive now checks gen before moving the shared schema. Deploys have less time to accidentally discover that a column wandered off.
gist.summary: Production CI now runs gen's Test and Typecheck in a new test-gen job before the shared database migration, leaving deploy-gen as a cached install-and-deploy step that completes in roughly 30 seconds instead of creating a roughly 2.5-minute schema mismatch window.
gist.impact: Users get more reliable releases: gen's cached registry can span the migration-to-deploy window, while failing gen tests now stop migrations and the coupled enter, media, and gen release before the shared schema changes.
gist.visual_concept: A shared garden bed represents the database schema: Polli, wearing a tiny inspector hat, checks a code-plant with a clipboard before the Monitor Robot gently replants it. A retro terminal shows a green test checkmark, while small connected garden paths represent the coordinated gen, enter, and media release.
